title: Devanagari — consonants
description: Thirty-three consonants plus the dotted letters for borrowed sounds. They are arranged by where in the mouth they are made, in rows of five: plain, breathy, voiced, voiced-breathy, nasal. The order is the dictionary order.

cards.back: k as in skip — no puff of air
cards.note: velar row: क ख ग घ ङ

cards.back: k with a puff of air, as in kick

cards.note: almost never written on its own

cards.back: ch as in church, no puff
cards.note: palatal row: च छ ज झ ञ

cards.back: ch with a puff of air
hard t, tongue curled back to the roof of the mouth
cards.note: retroflex row: ट ठ ड ढ ण — the sound English speakers hear as an Indian t

cards.back: hard t with a puff of air
hard d with a breathy release
n with the tongue curled back
soft t, tongue against the teeth, as in Spanish or French
cards.note: dental row: त थ द ध न

cards.back: soft t with a puff of air
soft d, tongue against the teeth
soft d with a breathy release
p as in spin — no puff
cards.note: labial row: प फ ब भ म

cards.back: p with a puff of air, as in pin
tapped r, as in Spanish pero

cards.note: in speech the same as श

cards.back: q from the back of the throat
cards.note: dotted letters carry Persian, Arabic and English sounds

cards.back: gargled g, as in French r

cards.note: बड़ा baṛā big, लड़का laṛkā boy

cards.back: flapped hard r with a breathy release
ksh — a conjunct that is taught as a letter
tr — conjunct of त and र
gy — conjunct of ज and ञ, said gya in Hindi
